solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Poor actors given boot finally and called "impaired"

parts.note: hams are actors who overplay their parts badly

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word boot

parts.note: rang or rung on the telephone means called

explanation.surface: Bad actors, given the boot, complain that they have been called impaired.
explanation.definitionFit: To be hamstrung is to be crippled or severely hampered, so impaired is a close synonym.

clue.text: Women's place to run after male? The opposite!

indicators.note: the clue first says run comes after male; the opposite order puts the runner first and the male letter last

parts.note: to hare is to run fast

explanation.surface: A man asks where the women's quarters are, then says to run after a man, or rather the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' would put HARE after M; 'The opposite!' flips that order so HARE comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A harem is the separate part of a Muslim household reserved for wives and female relatives.

clue.text: Acting as e.g. bishop in mitre, sing rousingly

indicators.note: rousingly suggests the letters of 'in mitre, sing' are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: A bishop wearing his mitre sings with gusto during a service.
explanation.definitionFit: Ministering means performing the duties of a clergyman, which is what a bishop does in church.

clue.text: Finest clothes motorists get into eventually?

parts.note: top means best or finest
gear is informal for clothes

explanation.surface: Drivers dress up in their best outfits once they finally reach their destination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finest clothes' reads as one phrase, a second definition, but it is the two pieces of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Drivers shift up through the ratios until they reach the highest one, the last they engage on a journey.

clue.text: A French location around one lake without nasty development?

parts.note: un is the French for a

indicators.note: around says the place word wraps itself round the one and lake letters

parts.note: a spot is a place or location
I is the Roman numeral one
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A French beauty spot by a lake has escaped ugly building projects.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unspoilt is untouched and unharmed, so it has not been marred by unpleasant change or building.

clue.text: End of sleeping? Wake up and grumble

indicators.note: End of picks the closing letter of the word sleeping

parts.note: to rouse someone is to wake them up

explanation.surface: Someone whose sleep is ended, woken up abruptly, starts complaining.
explanation.definitionFit: To grouse is to complain in a grumbling, moaning way; the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Cardinal is in taxi for return journey

indicators.note: a return journey goes back the way it came, so the combined letters are read backwards
in puts the word is inside the taxi word

parts.note: a cab is a taxi

explanation.surface: A senior churchman takes a taxi for the trip home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' looks like the prelate in red, but it is the adjective meaning fundamental; 'for return journey' turns the whole cab-and-is assembly round.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal as an adjective means chief or fundamental, as in cardinal rules, so it matches basic.

clue.text: Part of Australia maybe with unusual language to convey code of honour

parts.note: the bush is the rural backcountry of Australia, given with maybe as one example
Ido is an invented international language derived from Esperanto, hence unusual

explanation.surface: Someone in the Outback, speaking an odd tongue, passes on a code of honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Bushido is the samurai ethic of Japan, a strict code of loyalty and honourable conduct.

clue.text: Jump. missing footing, and slide

indicators.note: in a down entry the footing is the bottom letter, and missing says that last letter goes

parts.note: to skip is to jump lightly

explanation.surface: A jumper loses his footing and slides away.
explanation.definitionFit: To ski is to glide or slide over snow on long runners.

clue.text: US President not entirely intelligent to come down to earth

indicators.note: not entirely means the intelligent word loses its final letter

parts.note: clever means intelligent
to land is to come down to the ground

explanation.surface: A not-so-bright American president is told to come down to earth.
explanation.walkthrough: Grover Cleveland was the 22nd and 24th President of the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Grover Cleveland is an example of a president of the United States, serving two separate terms.

clue.text: Manage at university — so don't ***-** debts?

parts.note: to run something is to manage it
up means in residence at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: Advice to a student: manage your money at university so you avoid accumulating debts.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a fill-in-the-blank: the missing words complete the phrase about letting debts pile up.
explanation.definitionFit: To run up debts is to accumulate them, so the blanked phrase is completed by the answer.

clue.text: One may provide deal in beds with strong support externally

indicators.note: externally says the support word sits on the outside of the beds word

parts.note: the spine is the body's main support
cots are small beds

explanation.surface: Someone recommends a firm mattress with strong back support for a deal on beds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deal' here is not a bargain but softwood timber.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scots pine is a common conifer whose timber is sold as deal, a pine or fir softwood.

clue.text: Chemistry graduate maybe who has seen soft ceramic as a possibility

indicators.note: as a possibility suggests the letters of 'seen soft ceramic' are one possible rearrangement among many

explanation.surface: A chemistry graduate who has studied soft ceramics considers them a possible material.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemistry graduate may hold a master's degree in science, such as an MSc, so the degree is one example.

clue.text: Diplomacy that is set up in country: you've got stuck in

indicators.note: in puts the reversed letters inside the country word

parts.note: a nation is a country

indicators.note: stuck in says the word got is wedged between the reversed letters
in a down entry set up means read upwards, so the two letters are reversed

explanation.surface: A diplomat says that, in this country, you just have to get stuck in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns IE into EI; GOT is 'stuck in' it to give EGOTI, which goes 'in' NATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Negotiation is discussion aimed at reaching agreement, the core activity of diplomacy.

clue.text: Cheerlessly, unexcitedly cramping listener

indicators.note: cramping means confining, so the first word encloses the listener word

parts.note: drily means in a dry, matter-of-fact, unexcited way
the ear is the organ one listens with

explanation.surface: A lecture delivered without cheer and dully, cramping the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Drearily means in a dull, gloomy, depressing manner, which is the same as cheerlessly.

clue.text: Having grabbed key, daughter ran out and went downhill?

indicators.note: having grabbed means the daughter-and-ran-out letters hold the key letters inside them

parts.note: ended means finished or ran out
Esc is the escape key on a keyboard

explanation.surface: A daughter grabs the key and runs out of the house, heading down the hill.
explanation.definitionFit: Descended means went down, and going downhill is one way of descending, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Snake biting girl, no end upset, in Italian house

indicators.note: biting means the snake word closes round the other letters

parts.note: a boa is a large constricting snake

indicators.note: upset says the three remaining letters are knocked over into a new order
no end says the word girl loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A snake bites a girl in an Italian mansion and she is extremely upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end' leaves GIR, 'upset' rearranges that to RGI, which the boa is 'biting'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Borgias were a powerful Renaissance Italian family, and house here means a noble dynasty.

clue.text: Island not traced? It's given name, turning up in map book

indicators.note: in places the reversed letters inside the map book word

parts.note: an atlas is a book of maps

indicators.note: in a down entry turning up means the letters are read upwards, reversed

parts.note: read as 'it has', so IT is given the next letter

explanation.surface: A legendary island that cannot be traced is given a name in an atlas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' makes NTI from IT + N.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlantis is the legendary sunken island never found, so no map can trace it, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Yours truly's shout of exultation after quiet dance

indicators.note: after places the setter-and-shout letters behind the quiet letters

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
yours truly is the setter, so yours truly is becomes I'm
my! is an exclamation of surprise or delight

explanation.surface: The setter whoops with delight after a quiet dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The shimmy is a lively dance in which the body shakes, popular in the 1920s.

clue.text: Detective has month in Paris, given welcome after losing heart

parts.note: mai is French for May

indicators.note: losing heart means the welcome word drops one of its central letters

parts.note: to greet is to welcome

explanation.surface: A detective spends a month in Paris, welcomed but downhearted.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspector Maigret is Georges Simenon's fictional Paris police detective.

clue.text: Groovy drunk eats dirt

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters of 'eats dirt' are staggering into a new order

explanation.surface: A hip drunkard eats dirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Groovy' looks like slang for cool but means having grooves.
explanation.definitionFit: Striated means marked with parallel grooves or lines, which is literally groovy.

clue.text: Naive female at home, sincere, not trendy

indicators.note: in also means trendy, so not trendy says those two letters are removed from the sincere word

parts.note: genuine means sincere
in means at home

explanation.surface: A simple young woman at home is sincere but unfashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingenue is an innocent, unsophisticated young woman, especially as a stock stage role.

clue.text: Follow notice, hugged by escort

indicators.note: hugged by means the notice letters are held inside the escort word

parts.note: to show someone out or in is to escort them
an ad is a notice or advertisement

explanation.surface: Someone told to follow a notice is embraced by their escort.
explanation.definitionFit: To shadow someone is to follow them closely and secretly.

clue.text: He. engaging with us all, managed a style of communication we understand

definitions.text: a style of communication we understand

indicators.note: managed suggests the letters of 'He', 'engaging' and 'us all' are handled and rearranged

explanation.surface: A man engaging with everyone used a manner of speaking that we can follow.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the language of the puzzle itself, so it is a way of communicating its readers understand.

clue.text: I'm volatile in that place, the first to rise up

indicators.note: in a down entry rise up means go towards the top, so the last letter climbs to become the first

parts.note: there means in that place

explanation.surface: A boastful person declares themselves volatile, the first to rise up anywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The final E of THERE 'rises up' to the top of the entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Ether is a highly volatile liquid that evaporates readily, so it can speak of itself as volatile.

clue.text: Give the lie to smear

definitions.meaning: to show a claim to be false or doubtful

explanation.definitionFit: Discredit means both to cast doubt on a claim and to harm someone's reputation, matching each definition.

clue.text: Thus belonging to the upper echelons makes a bit of money

parts.note: so means thus
U means upper-class, characteristic of the upper classes

explanation.surface: Being upper-class supposedly earns a small coin.
explanation.definitionFit: The sou was an old French coin of low value, hence a small bit of money.

clue.text: Half of the people in our street make a beastly noise

indicators.note: half of takes the front five of the ten letters

parts.note: the people living in our street are our neighbours

explanation.surface: Half the residents on our road make a horrible racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beastly' looks like 'awful' but means made by a beast.
explanation.definitionFit: To neigh is to make the cry of a horse, an animal's or beast's noise.

clue.text: Uncertainty makes engineers abandon temporary fortification

indicators.note: abandon means the engineers letters leave the fortification word

parts.note: a redoubt is a temporary outwork or fortification
RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army's engineering corps

explanation.surface: Engineers, uncertain, abandon a temporary fort.
explanation.definitionFit: Doubt is a state of being unsure, which is uncertainty.

clue.text: First person meeting severe monarch may be a North American

parts.note: we is the first person plural pronoun
stern means severe
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the British monarch

explanation.surface: Someone meets a severe king and wonders whether he is from North America.
explanation.definitionFit: A westerner is someone from the western world, and a North American is one example.
